chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Mushamil, and from Ibn Ribat, from Mushamil, all of them from Abu Baseer who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read out to me regarding the obligatory shares of inheritance: A woman who passed away and left her husband. He said: 'The wealth, all of it is for the husband.' And (regarding) a man who passed away and left his wife, he said: 'For the wife is the one-quarter, and whatever remains, so it is for the Imam.'

key_terms.فَلِلْإِمَامِ: so it is for the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a widow if her husband dies leaving no other heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ibaqa' (residual inheritance) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam acts as the sole heir for the spouse when no other relatives exist. While the wife receives one-quarter of the estate, the remaining three-quarters escheat to the Imam, reflecting the Imam's role as the custodian of the community's wealth in the absence of direct lineage. This ruling underscores the unique status of the Imam as the ultimate heir in the absence of other kin, a concept distinct from some Sunni schools that may distribute the remainder among other categories.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Rabat, from Muhammad Bin Sukeyn and Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Mushmail, and from Ibn Rabat, from Mushmail, all of them from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> read out to me regarding the Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance), a woman who passed away and left her husband. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth, all of it is for the husband’. And (about a man who died and left his wife (only), he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the wife is the one-quarter and whatever remains, so it is for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and Ali ibn abu Hamzah from Mushma‘il and ibn Ribat from Mushma‘il all of them from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once read for me (from the book) on the issue of ordained shares of inheritance the following: ‘A woman dies and leaves behind her husband,’ he (the Imam) said, ‘The entire legacy belongs to him. If a man dies and leaves behind his wife, he (the Imam) said that one- fourth belongs to her and the rest belongs to the Imam.’”
